meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Who decided Owen gets a zero, and was he heard first?
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. On what basis?

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
11:52 and 11:58, I'm writing that down. Kids write in one place and paste into another, Hale. That shows when it was pasted, not who wrote it.
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
Fine. Whatever happens next, this stays off his record and it stays quiet. What else do you have?
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
Seventeen-year-olds misquote Shakespeare all the time, Hale. A wrong line in an essay is a mistake, not a crime.
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
Okay. So what are you putting on the table, and under which section?
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
Students change their argument between an outline and an essay; that's what an outline is for. And you didn't answer me: what are you proposing?

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
That's 4.4, in writing, tonight. He'll do the rewrite to put this behind him, Hale, not because he did anything. Private, before December 1, and nothing on his file.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
I'll confirm with him tonight. Put Thursday the twelfth in that email.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
cc: Principal, Elbow Crossing High School

Hale,

In today's meeting you agreed that, under procedure 4.4, Owen will complete a private supervised rewrite after school on Thursday, November 12, not in front of his class and before December 1, that its mark will replace the zero, and that nothing will be placed on his record. I still require that agreement from you in writing, including your commitment that nothing goes on his file. I expect it tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Last position: she agreed to a private supervised rewrite on Thursday, November 12, and she still wants your written promise tonight that nothing goes on his file; that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and you reached it well before her call.
What moved her: You showed the version history with its times and then answered her paste-from-elsewhere defence by inviting Owen to bring a dated draft, which gave her something specific she could check and nothing to argue with.
What cost ground: Very little; the outline comparison came right after she asked what you were proposing, so it read as a dodge and she pressed harder, though it cost you no position.
What she never said: One night in October she came downstairs at 1 AM, saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history put the whole essay between 11:31 PM and 11:58 PM on October 28, the night before it was due, which came very close to that kind of late night, and while her memory proves nothing about this essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asked what you were proposing and under which section, put 4.4 on the table right then and hold the outline in reserve in case she pushed back on the rewrite.
